verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance publishes a public, keyless OpenAPI document for its v3 API. The API uses OAuth client credentials, rate-limit headers, and idempotency keys, and the probe confirmed registered-agent-deliveries endpoints. However, those endpoints cover service-of-process deliveries rather than registered-agent appointments, entity-record endpoints are not explicitly evidenced, and write access requires a capability Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant. Missing for 10: confirmed entity-record and registered-agent-appointment endpoints, self-serve create/update/delete access, independent hands-on corroboration of real API use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read or manage entity records and registered-agent appointments programmatically through a documented public API

citations.quote: a public, keyless OpenAPI document for the Harbor Compliance API (OAuth-authenticated at runtime)
Creating, updating, and deleting resources requires additional capabilities which Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant to your account
